fsm_states_request.name: IDLE
fsm_states_request.description: MCmd=IDLE; no request presented this cycle.

fsm_states_request.name: REQ
fsm_states_request.description: Master drives a valid MCmd (+MAddr and, for a non-datahandshake write, MData/MByteEn). The request handshake completes on the cycle MCmd is valid and SCmdAccept is asserted.

fsm_states_request.name: REQ_WAIT
fsm_states_request.description: Slave holds SCmdAccept deasserted; the master holds the request stable until the slave accepts.

fsm_states_datahandshake.name: DH_VALID
fsm_states_datahandshake.description: Master asserts MDataValid with MData/MDataByteEn; the beat is accepted when SDataAccept is asserted.

fsm_states_datahandshake.name: DH_WAIT
fsm_states_datahandshake.description: Slave holds SDataAccept deasserted; the master holds the write-data beat stable.

fsm_states_response.name: RESP
fsm_states_response.description: Slave drives SResp (DVA/FAIL/ERR) and SData for a read; the response handshake completes when SResp is non-NULL and MRespAccept is asserted.

fsm_states_response.name: RESP_WAIT
fsm_states_response.description: Master holds MRespAccept deasserted; the slave holds the response stable.

fsm_hints.trigger: A transfer begins when the master drives a non-IDLE MCmd with a valid MAddr; the request completes when SCmdAccept is asserted.
fsm_hints.rule: The master must hold the request (and, in the datahandshake phase, the write-data beat) stable until the corresponding accept (SCmdAccept / SDataAccept) is asserted; the slave must hold the response stable until MRespAccept is asserted.
fsm_hints.abort: There is no protocol-level abort; a phase simply stalls while the corresponding accept signal is deasserted (or a thread is busy).

anti_deadlock_rule: Each accept signal (SCmdAccept / SDataAccept / MRespAccept) must eventually assert so the corresponding phase can complete; SThreadBusy/MThreadBusy back-pressure individual threads without stalling the whole socket. When an accept signal is not configured, that phase completes in a single cycle.
thread_concurrency_rule: Transfers on different threads (MThreadID/SThreadID) have no ordering constraint; within one thread, transfers complete in order unless tags (MTagID/STagID) permit out-of-order responses.
